name: Reporting post office availability issues
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person sought help reporting a USPS post office for failing to open on time. The core issue was that at 9:23 AM on a Thursday, the facility's phone system routed calls directly to voicemail with a message stating the call was outside normal business hours of 8:30 AM onwards — a direct contradiction that the person recognized as strong documented evidence of a facility operations failure.

Claude provided a tiered set of reporting options: filing via the USPS online complaint form at emailus.usps.com (selecting the USPS Locations category covering hours and access), calling 1-800-ASK-USPS to speak with a representative or obtain the station manager's contact, and escalating to the Postal Regulatory Commission at prc.gov/contact for pattern-based complaints requiring a formal USPS response within 45 days. Claude emphasized that the voicemail contradiction was the person's strongest piece of evidence and advised documenting it specifically.

The person then encountered a notable technical issue: pasting the emailus.usps.com URL directly into a browser address bar produced an error, but navigating to the identical URL through the USPS app worked successfully. Claude explained this as a session cookie or authentication token requirement — the USPS contact form requires an active session established through the app or main site navigation before it will load, and direct URL entry bypasses that session initialization. The practical workaround identified was to always access the form via the app or from the USPS homepage rather than direct linking. The conversation ended with Claude asking whether the person had successfully submitted the complaint.

Here are your options for reporting this, ranked by how direct and effective they are:

**Most immediate — File online via the USPS "Email Us" form**
Go to **emailus.usps.com** and select the category for USPS Locations (covering access, hours, and appearance). This goes directly into their Customer 360 complaint tracking system and gets routed to staff who can act on it.

**By phone**
Call **1-800-ASK-USPS** (1-800-275-8777) to speak with a representative. You can also use this number to ask for contact info for your local station manager. Talking to the station manager directly is often the fastest path to resolution for a facility-level issue like this.

**Escalation — Postal Regulatory Commission**
If this is a pattern rather than a one-off incident, you can submit a complaint through the PRC's contact form. They document the issue, can forward it to USPS for investigation, and USPS is required to respond within 45 days — with the PRC receiving a copy to verify the problem was handled appropriately. That's at **prc.gov/contact**.

**For the complaint itself**, be specific: include the facility's name and address, the posted opening time, the time you arrived and found it closed, and whether this has happened before if you know. The more documentation you have, the harder it is for USPS to dismiss it as a one-time anomaly.

GAO's analysis of USPS's fiscal year 2020 residential complaints data found a total of 10.7-million residential customer complaints were reported by about 5.6 percent of the residential addresses USPS served. Most of these complaints—69 percent—were related to packages, such as missing or delayed packages. GAO found that about 21 percent of addresses that reported a complaint had more than one complaint. Of those addresses, a majority of complaints occurred less than one month apart, and many had two complaints with the same USPS-assigned root cause.

USPS officials are currently reviewing whether the root cause field is accurately capturing the cause of a complaint. Across USPS, multiple officials told GAO they use the C360 system's reporting capabilities to access, review, and analyze complaints data.
